clue.text: Farm worker firm with stick, collaring head of heifer

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: collaring means grabbing round the neck, so the stick goes round the next piece

parts.note: a wand is a slender stick

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ranch hand, firm and armed with a stick, grabs a young cow by the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collaring' is the container signal: the stick grips the heifer's initial like a hand on a collar; 'with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowhand is a labourer who tends cattle on a ranch or farm.

clue.text: Run out of conversation? A touch of loquacity's an asset

indicators.note: out of means the run letter is taken away from the talk

parts.note: chatter is idle conversation
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: a touch is a small first contact, so just the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone who has run dry of talk finds a little chattiness a real asset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from CHATTER, giving CHATTE; then L from 'A touch of loquacity's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal property, something owned of value.

clue.text: All dinner money will be needed for healthy food?

parts.note: the whole is all of something
dinner is a meal
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A parent warns that the whole dinner allowance will go on health food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be needed for' only links pieces and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaves made from unrefined flour are seen as wholesome fare.

clue.text: In which you'll see some war enacted?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A venue where battles are staged for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a place in which a battle may be watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiatorial combats were staged before crowds in an amphitheatre.

clue.text: Shame recording needs engineer's last retouch

parts.note: a disc is a recording, a record

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to edit is to revise or retouch

explanation.surface: An embarrassing recording needs a final touch-up from the sound engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' only joins pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit is to disgrace, bringing dishonour on someone.

clue.text: Wonderful magazine I cry unceasingly

indicators.note: without ceasing means the word is not allowed to finish, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to call is to cry out

explanation.surface: A reader gushes that the magazine is so wonderful it keeps them crying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unceasingly' cuts the final letter from CALL, leaving CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something magical seems enchanting, as wonderful as sorcery.

clue.text: Lawman? Oxford detective's not right

indicators.note: not tells us the following letter is removed

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the fictional detective of TV novels set in Oxford

explanation.surface: Is the Oxford sleuth a lawman, or is that wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a British TV detective based in Oxford; removing R gives the lawgiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses received the Ten Commandments and gave the law to Israel.

clue.text: State of course? Very keen on making investigation

parts.note: the going is the ground condition of a racecourse
to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it

explanation.surface: Asked about racing conditions, a fan admits to being an enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The going' is the racing term for how firm or soft a course is.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a matter is to examine it closely.

clue.text: 100 felonies — batch that's upset this officer?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: upset means overturned and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hundred crimes in one go would upset a senior policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges C with FELONIES and BATCH; the police chief is suitably dismayed.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a British county police force holds this rank.

clue.text: Subsequently adopting new name for lamp

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Afterwards a new name was adopted for the lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts N inside LATER, giving LANTER; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp with a protective case.

clue.text: In heaven, and a little free of guilt?

parts.note: heaven is traditionally up above
a suspicion of something is a tiny trace of it

explanation.surface: Someone in paradise, and only slightly blameless, wonders about their status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two pieces; 'a suspicion of garlic' shows the trace sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond reproach is not even suspected of wrongdoing, hence innocent.

clue.text: See 9
The suffix for 'lizard 'is in the lexicon

parts.note: taken as written
-saurus, from Greek for lizard, ends names like tyrannosaurus

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the ending for lizard words appears in the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in the' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of words grouped by meaning, a kind of word list.

clue.text: Foreman almost making mistake

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: a gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: The site boss nearly commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is British slang for a works foreman; 'almost' drops its last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing slip.

clue.text: City has prominence, according to rumour

indicators.note: rumour is what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: one who leads is out in front, prominent

explanation.surface: Gossip says a particular city stands out above the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEDS is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major English city in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Links Aran with development of island

indicators.note: development reworks the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Golf links on Aran are developed into an island resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges LINKSARAN; ARAN is a group of Irish islands, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lankan describes things from the island nation off India.

clue.text: What provokes monk? Party dress (short) is liable to

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a mini is a short dress
can, as in 'it can rain here', means is liable to

explanation.surface: What tempts a monk? A short party dress might well do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question and answer form one picture; 'What provokes' only sets up the scene and the definition is just 'monk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominicans are friars of the order founded by St Dominic, so a religious brother.

clue.text: Stop here for busses?

parts.note: busses is an old spelling of kisses; a sprig of plant hung up where couples pause to kiss

explanation.walkthrough: 'busses' looks like the vehicles, but buss means kiss; the hanging Christmas plant is where you stop for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition says people under this Christmas plant must kiss.

clue.text: See 7 down
Softens and fades around the end, on reflection

indicators.note: around tells us the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to pale is to fade

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: Something softens and fades at the finish, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' is the reversal signal and 'around' the container signal; 'the end' is a noun here, not a closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease or mitigate pain without curing it.

clue.text: River with level of water fit to drink

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the water table is the level of groundwater

explanation.surface: A river whose water level is high enough to drink from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is safe for drinking.

clue.text: One has three bridge players surrounded by men

indicators.note: surrounded by means the players go inside the men

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
bridge players sit as North, South, East and West; W, N and E are three

explanation.surface: Someone holds a hand, with three card players hemmed in by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for 'men'; bridge players are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something.

clue.text: Composer with baton-choir forgetting error

parts.note: a baton is a rod

indicators.note: forgetting means a part of the word is left out

parts.note: a choir is a body of singers
a sin is an error or wrong

explanation.surface: A composer with baton forgives the choir its mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes SIN from SINGERS, leaving GERS; Richard Rodgers wrote musicals with Hammerstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Rodgers composed Oklahoma! and The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Bill left a drum

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a drum and the invoice for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of Indian hand drums.

clue.text: See 2 down
Assigned new collection of cello data

indicators.note: a new collection means these letters are gathered afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Fresh cello figures are distributed to researchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new collection of' signals rearranging CELLODATA.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to allot or give out a share.

clue.text: Gather service supports article

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means lies underneath the other piece

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A church service backs a newspaper article on gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts MASS below A in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to accumulate or collect.

clue.text: Annoyed economy's on the rise?

parts.note: a cut is an economy, a saving
up means rising

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that the cost-saving drive is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking CUT to UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut up means being distressed or upset.

clue.text: Place to eat literally linked to Holmes (but not Watson)

definitions.meaning: a ... where the morning meal is taken

definitions.text: literally linked to Holmes (but not Watson)
definitions.meaning: This is that literary Holmes, not Sherlock with his Watson

explanation.surface: A dining spot tied to the great detective, though without his sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holmes' tempts towards Sherlock; the parenthesis warns off him, pointing to the American essayist Oliver Wendell Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a household dining surface for the morning meal, and the title setting of Holmes's essays.

clue.text: See 25
Stops loans head of library banned

indicators.note: banned means the named letter is shut out of the word

parts.note: lendings are things lent, loans

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The library halts its loans after the chief librarian is barred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned' removes the L from 'head of library' from LENDINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Endings are conclusions, the points where things cease.

clue.text: Train, having left journalism?

parts.note: ex means former, someone who has left a role
the press is journalism collectively

explanation.surface: A reporter catches a train after quitting the newspaper trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a noun: a fast service that stops at few stations.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast train with few stops.
